package.title: What If You Got Back the 26 Years You Spend Asleep?
description: Eight hours a night, every night. What if you got all of it back?
The math: 8 hours out of 24 is a third of your life. By 30, that's 30 × 365 × 8 = 87,600 hours, or ten whole years. By 80, it's 26 years and 8 months.

The real part: in 2009, Ying-Hui Fu's lab at UCSF found a mother and daughter with a tiny change in a gene called DEC2. They naturally sleep about six hours a night and wake up rested. Nobody can safely go without sleep entirely.
Would you take the 26 years? Tell me in the comments.
sources: He Y. et al. (2009), The transcriptional repressor DEC2 regulates sleep length in mammals. Science 325: 866–870. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1174443
package.pinned: Would you take the 26 years, knowing everyone you love is asleep for a third of them?
alt_titles: You Never Sleep Again. By 30, You've Gained 10 Years.
